extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, policymakers, Congress, agency staff, and external IP stakeholders (patent applicants, practitioners, and partner governments)
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpts from the USPTO 2021 Performance and Accountability Report describing program-level performance criteria, organizational effectiveness standards, IT/product delivery goals, telework and workforce metrics, cybersecurity expectations, and patent-centric delivery improvements. Useful for assessing agency performance and program design in support of patent operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional improvements of IP office administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional improvements of intellectual property (IP) office administration for advancing IP rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of four performance criteria used to assess progress in prioritized countries (Table 22). Progress on this criterion contributes to the percentage of prioritized countries for which IP country teams have made progress on at least three of the four performance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional improvements of IP enforcement entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional improvements of IP enforcement entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a core performance criterion in Table 22 to evaluate country-level progress on strengthening enforcement capabilities; counted alongside the other three criteria to determine overall progress for prioritized countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements in IP laws and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvements in IP laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A primary evaluation dimension for country teams (Table 22). The USPTO monitors changes (e.g., draft laws, regulations, guidance) and provides comments to help ensure effective protection for U.S. rights holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of government–to–government cooperative mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment of government–to–government cooperative mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as the fourth core performance criterion for prioritized countries; progress on establishing cooperative mechanisms (e.g., MOUs, joint programs) is tracked as part of overall country progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress metric: Countries meeting ≥3 of 4 criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of prioritized countries for which IP country teams have made progress on at least three of the four performance criteria (Table 22).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets are set (e.g., 66% for FY 2018 onward) and actuals reported annually. Note: target was updated in FY 2018 to reflect a decrease in number of prioritized countries from four to three.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP Attaché activity reporting and success tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative tracking of attaché activities (e.g., number of participants engaged, weekly activity reports submitted, identifiable successes reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate IP Attaché Program effectiveness (example figures: 7,791 participants; 519 weekly activity reports; 71 identifiable successes). These metrics can overlap with other reporting (e.g., GIPA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance management system effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness of the performance management system measured by whether it: draws distinctions between high- and low-level performers; uses clearly defined standards and expectations at all organizational and individual levels; acknowledges achievements via transparent reward and recognition; and links individual performance plans to organizational goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO uses these four characteristics as criteria for an effective system; training is provided to managers to ensure consistent application. Metrics and examples: number of managers trained, sessions delivered, and alignment of individual plans to organizational goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment outreach and employer branding
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruitment outreach should emphasize the USPTO mission and core organizational values and use targeted digital campaigns and branded materials to engage both active and passive job seekers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes leveraging social media channels (LinkedIn, Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube), hosting targeted Twitter chats for mission-critical occupations, and special outreach (e.g., veteran-targeted events, HBCU events). Measured by hires, follower growth, and event participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veteran hiring and targeted recruitment metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Track and measure veteran representation in hiring (e.g., percentage of patent examiners and other hires who are veterans) and participation in veteran-specific recruitment events and campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 7% of patent examiners and 17% of all other hires were veterans in FY 2021; participated in 18 veteran-specific recruitment events and launched targeted advertising and content featuring veteran employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development and training program outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate career development programs (Career Coaching, After Work Education, Upward Mobility Program, APEX, Enterprise-Wide Mentoring) by participation, coaching hours, program completions, and career advancement outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of measurable program data: number of coaches trained, employee-clients and coaching hours, AWE participants, UMP participants, APEX enrollments, mentoring pairs and participants. Use these figures to assess impact on recruitment/retention and promotion readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for voluntary employee organizations (VEOs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide toolkits, templates, policies, event calendars, leadership contacts, and webinars to assist formation, governance, and programming of VEOs; use VEOs to promote cultural, social, and career-development activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations include regular Council of Leaders meetings, co-sponsorship of cultural programs, development of Employee Groups website and brochures, and virtual event participation; measure by number of VEOs, participation rates, and engagement metrics (e.g., newsletter subscribers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telework program benefits and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Telework programs should reduce the need for office space, enhance recruitment and retention, foster greater production and management efficiency, provide work flexibility and improved work-life balance, improve climate resiliency, and minimize environmental impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify benefits via metrics such as CO2 emissions avoided, miles not driven, gas savings, and participation counts. Use telework to ensure continuity during extreme weather or emergency situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telework eligibility and participation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Track percentage of positions eligible to telework and percentage of eligible employees participating (including permanent official telework agreements vs. mandatory pandemic telework).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: percentage eligible decreased slightly from 94.51% to 94.39% between FY 2020 and FY 2021; figures broken out by state and business unit. Use these metrics to assess program reach and inform eligibility revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telework Enhancement Act Program (TEAP) parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: TEAP permits full-time teleworkers to elect an official duty station greater than 50 miles from headquarters, waiving certain travel expense rights for a limited number of required trips back to headquarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure program participation (e.g., 3,079 employees in FY 2021) and track changes in duty station/residence patterns and waived travel reimbursements when evaluating program impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership development program design and success measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Leadership Academy components (Emerging Leaders Program, Supervisor Certificate Program, Ideal Leader Confidence Course, SES-level Apollo Leadership Experience) should develop leadership skills, be cohort-based, and have measurable outcomes (e.g., promotions, applications for supervisory roles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs were redesigned for virtual delivery; track cohort sizes, completions (e.g., 25 participants per ELP cohort), promotions and career advancement of graduates, and compliance with OPM requirements (e.g., SCP delivered within first year of supervisory status).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee engagement measurement and targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use agency-wide surveys (People Pulse, Gallup Q12 People Survey) to measure employee well-being and understanding of mission; track response rates and engagement mean scores across survey areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 46% response rate to People Pulse; 45% response to People Survey; engagement mean tracked on 1–5 scale and compared year-over-year with area-level improvements used to inform engagement strategy. Use survey data to identify return-to-office preferences and other workforce needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: IT delivery transformation goals (product-based model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition from project-based to product-based IT delivery to: focus on the full spectrum of IT delivery, link IT to agency strategies, align resources (capacity, funding, staff, contractors), enable decision-making at working level, communicate strategic vision and business value, articulate delivery plans, communicate resource capacity needs, highlight risks and interdependencies, and document technical boundaries for accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalize these goals via a product catalog, product roadmaps, prioritized business outcomes, and agile practices (e.g., Dojo training). Measure success by number of product teams trained, frequency of value delivery, and clarity of roadmaps and resource alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product catalog organization and product line definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize IT products into product lines (Patent Product Line, Trademark Product Line, Enterprise Business Product Line, Enterprise Infrastructure Product Line) grouping by service similarity, business value goals, and customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each product line should encompass products across the lifecycle (filing, examination, appeals, search, fees, maintenance, reporting for IP lines; enterprise functions for business lines) and include both legacy and modernized systems. Product roadmaps and prioritized outcomes are required for each product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Product Line scope and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Product Line encompasses products and components that deliver business value across the patent lifecycle: filing, examination, appeals, search, international data exchange, fees, maintenance, and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for stabilization, containment, retirement of legacy components, and modernization; measure by availability, performance, and the ability to support examiners, applicants, and international partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Product Line scope and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark Product Line encompasses products and components that deliver business value across the trademark lifecycle: filing, examination, appeals, search, international data exchange, fees, maintenance, and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar expectations as Patent Product Line with metrics on system stability, modernization progress, and stakeholder access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enterprise Business Product Line scope and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Enterprise Business Product Line includes products supporting fee collection/refunds, communications, financials, procurement, budgeting, HR, time and attendance, property and facilities, legal matters, data analytics, and business intelligence reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many solutions are configured/customized COTS; measure success by business continuity, cost-effectiveness, and ability to meet agency-wide business needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enterprise Infrastructure Product Line scope and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Enterprise Infrastructure Product Line (EIPL) provides essential technologies and services to staff and customers, focusing on being better, faster, cheaper while increasing security, availability, and resilience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes end-user services, platform services, infra/hosting (compute, data center, storage, cloud, network), delivery services (ITSM), security and compliance services, IT management services, and emerging technology. Measure by uptime, security posture, scalability, and cost metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity and risk management criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement emerging security technologies, security architecture, security operations best practices, and an improved risk management framework; integrate continuous and automated security at early software development stages and throughout product lifecycles; include supply chain risk management and prioritize remediation of high-value assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect cyclical identification, prioritization, and remediation of vulnerabilities; maintain a standard policy on time to remediation; transition products from end-of-support platforms to secure versions. Example outcome: 60% decrease in open POA&Ms for security vulnerabilities across products in FY 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents end-to-end systems improvement criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve patent prosecution tools (e.g., DAV, Docket Management, Official Correspondence tool, examiner search tool) to support updated examination time allotments, application routing, enhanced authoring/workflow, performance reporting, and scalable search capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track functional enhancements, migration of foreign collections (e.g., 70+ million image/text files with translations), stress and scalability testing for search algorithms, training coverage for examiners (e.g., 2,500+ trained), and development of troubleshooting and performance monitoring tools to support operational efficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enterprise search tool performance and scalability expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: New examiner search tool must be a modern, scalable enterprise search with acceptable search algorithm performance and scalability for the entire patent corps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize longer development timelines due to algorithm complexity; require stress testing, scaling corrective actions, addition of foreign collections, and phased training. Monitor deployment readiness via performance benchmarks and examiner training completion rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data set and documentation standards (AIPD)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIPD dataset should identify U.S. patents and pre-grant publications containing AI technology components, include the patent documents used to train the ML model, and be accompanied by a technical working paper that provides complete documentation for ease of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datasets must be well-documented to assist researchers and policymakers; include explicit descriptions of selection criteria, data fields, training materials, and usage notes to ensure reproducibility and interpretability.
